title: Can the EU and Canada forge a new partnership?
gist: PIIE argues von der Leyen's 'associate member' offer to Canada has no legal basis, but EU-Canada ties can deepen via full CETA ratification, critical minerals, defense procurement and CPTPP, as Carney diversifies away from the US ahead of the Oct 29-30 Montreal summit.

insights.claim: The term 'associate member' has no legal definition in the EU treaties, was absent from the draft speech circulated the day before, and surprised EU member states and Carney.
insights.speaker: Cecilia Malmström and Inu Manak
insights.so_what: Treat the offer as political signalling, not a legal path to single-market access.
insights.locator: The term "associate member" does not exist

insights.claim: Canada is not and will not become an EU candidate country, and full single-market access would require adopting the EU acquis, which Canada's close regulatory alignment with the US rules out.
insights.speaker: Cecilia Malmström and Inu Manak
insights.so_what: Limits how far EU-Canada integration can go beyond a traditional FTA.
insights.locator: CETA does not give Canada full access

insights.claim: Trade in goods and services between Canada and the EU is up 81% (EUR131 billion) since 2016, but goods trade was only about EUR92 billion in 2025 against $880 billion of Canada-US trade.
insights.speaker: Cecilia Malmström and Inu Manak
insights.so_what: Canada's trade pivot from the US has a large gap to close.

insights.claim: CETA remains only provisional because 10 EU member states have not ratified it, leaving investment protection rules inapplicable; upcoming elections in France, Greece and Poland and agricultural concerns make finalisation unlikely soon.
insights.speaker: Cecilia Malmström and Inu Manak
insights.so_what: Expect no near-term full CETA ratification; investment-protection upside is delayed.
insights.locator: One way to further CETA's potential

insights.claim: Canada has not filled its agreed EU beef export quota because of EU rules on hormone-treated meat, and a Canada-EU digital agreement on services trade is being negotiated.
insights.speaker: Cecilia Malmström and Inu Manak
insights.so_what: Agriculture remains the friction point in EU-Canada trade.

insights.claim: Canada is the first non-European country to join SAFE, the EU instrument for common defence procurement, and has been invited to European Political Community meetings.
insights.speaker: Cecilia Malmström and Inu Manak
insights.so_what: Canada is being integrated into European defence-industrial supply chains.
insights.locator: As proof of the close relation

insights.claim: An EU-Canada summit in Montreal on October 29-30 is the first meeting since the US-Canada trade war broke out this summer; the draft statement covers supply chains, energy, AI, critical minerals, defense and more but omits 'associate member' and CETA ratification.
insights.speaker: Cecilia Malmström and Inu Manak
insights.so_what: Expect broad but low-commitment outputs; watch for concrete critical-minerals and defense deals.

insights.claim: Pooling Canadian resources with European processing capacity under an agreement signed earlier this year on critical raw materials and rare earths could build scale and secure supply, but needs joint risk assessments and financial investment.
insights.speaker: Cecilia Malmström and Inu Manak
insights.so_what: Critical minerals is the most investable EU-Canada cooperation area.

insights.claim: A natural next step would be for the EU to join Canada and Asia-Pacific countries in the CPTPP, though nothing concrete has happened since early summer.
insights.speaker: Cecilia Malmström and Inu Manak
insights.so_what: An EU-CPTPP link would be a major trade-bloc shift but is not imminent.
